description: This database is stored in SQLite database format and contains metadata about GitHub repositories, including their declared programming languages, licenses, and repository-level statistics. It consists of three tables:
Name of the GitHub repository in `owner/repo` format.
Programming language(s) used in the repository, represented in natural language format.
Name of the GitHub repository in `owner/repo` format.
License identifier associated with the repository (e.g., `apache-2.0`, `mit`).
Name of the GitHub repository in `owner/repo` format.
Number of users watching the repository on GitHub.
This database is stored in DuckDB format and contains GitHub repository artifacts, including file contents, commit history, and file-level metadata. It consists of three tables:
Identifier of the file blob in the repository.
The file content (textual data). For large or binary files, this may contain placeholders or truncated values.
Name of the repository where the file resides, in `owner/repo` format.
Reference name (e.g., branch or commit SHA).
Path of the file within the repository.
If the file is a symlink, indicates the symlink target path.
Natural language description summarizing the file’s metadata (derived from original size, binary, copies, and mode fields).
Unique identifier (SHA) of the commit.
SHA identifier of the commit’s associated tree object.
One or more parent commit SHAs (JSON-like format for merge commits).
JSON-like object containing author information (name, email, timestamp).
JSON-like object containing committer information (name, email, timestamp).
Short subject line of the commit message.
Full commit message.
Additional metadata fields attached to the commit (JSON-like).
JSON-like structure representing file changes introduced by the commit.
Indicator if the difference data is truncated.
Repository name in `owner/repo` format.
Encoding format of the commit data (if applicable).
Name of the GitHub repository in `owner/repo` format.
Reference name (branch or commit SHA) at which the file metadata is recorded.
Path of the file within the repository.
File mode (e.g., normal file, executable, symlink).
Identifier of the file blob.
If the file is a symlink, the target path it points to.
